A Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) is a network that maps one field to another by mixing information in the frequency domain [@li2021fourier].
Here it is trained as an inverse for the Gray-Scott model: given an observed or drawn late pattern, it returns either an earlier state or the parameter fields that grow the pattern.
It answers in a single forward pass, about 0.1 s for 20 scenes, where the [Diffusion Controller](../diffusion-controller/index.qmd) needs about 5 minutes for 8 guided draws.

Each grid size was used for a different task, so the scores below are not comparable across grids.
The score is the re-simulation error: the distance between the target and what the solver grows from the FNO's answer.

## 16 × 16: an earlier state from a few pixels

The FNO sees 50 pixels of the pattern at step 300 and returns the state at step 50.
Trained on the start state alone it averages over all possible starts; trained on how well its answer re-simulates, it does much better.
After the same solver polish as the diffusion model, the two are tied (the FNO is lower on 12 of 20 scenes).

{{< include charts/grid16.html >}}

On a second set of 618 tasks, an FNO and a diffusion denoiser built on the same backbone were trained side by side: the FNO solved 60% of tasks (best of 8 draws below 0.1), the denoiser 37%.

## 32 × 32: parameter maps for drawn shapes

From a fixed central blob, the FNO returns the feed, kill and diffusivity maps so that the pattern at step 300 matches a target shape.
Supervised training alone works on held-out masks grown by Gray-Scott but rarely on drawn shapes.
Continuing training through the solver, starting from the supervised weights, makes most draws succeed; MCC, the Matthews correlation between target and result, of at least 0.8 counts as success.

{{< include charts/grid32.html >}}

Two caveats.
Training through the solver from random weights collapsed: every answer killed the pattern, and nothing succeeded.
And the successful kill maps partly mirror the target shape, the trivial answer (correlation −0.54 to −0.61 with the target); the L and X shapes are never solved.

## 64 × 64: further back in time

The FNO sees 800 of the 4,096 pixels and returns the state 250 steps earlier.
Adding small local kernels to the published FNO layer cut the error by 40%, and fine-tuning on the re-simulated future cut it further, with no pattern dying.
Going further back fails: at 500 steps the error stays high, and at 1000 steps every recovered start dies out.

{{< include charts/grid64.html >}}

The reason is the same at every long horizon.
A one-pass answer trained on the start state is the average of all starts that fit, which has about half the true amplitude, and a Gray-Scott pattern below its sustaining amplitude dies.
Past about 250 steps the solver has to be part of the training objective.
